newsitem.title: USA: PSA seeks SEC view on mortgage-backed reporting.
newsitem.headline: PSA seeks SEC view on mortgage-backed reporting.

text.p: The nation's leading bond trade association, PSA, on Monday said it will seek the views of the Securities and Exchange Commission and others on its proposals to improve performance reporting in private mortage-backed and asset-backed securities issues.
PSA said next month it will release its proposals in a discussion paper to the SEC, other regulators and market participants.

The group is seeking improvements in remittance information, or the data reported periodically on the collection and distribution of cash flows from receivables and assets which support payments on these securities issues.

This information from federal agency mortgage securities issues is available in a standardized, automated format directly from the agencies or from private information vendors. But the data on private securities deals is "neither as standardized or automated as in the case of federal housing agency securities," PSA said.

"As a result, the dealer community, investors, analysts and other market participants expend considerable costs and manpower in order to obtain accurate and timely remittance information for non-agency (securities)," PSA warned.
In its discussion paper, PSA said it will recommend that minimum remittance reporting standards be set for private securities issues.
The group will recommend that the reporting be done electronically rather than manually and that standarized calculations and definitions be established.

Further, such information should be available from one central source, possibly through Internet, PSA will recommend. But the group cautioned that its proposals should be weighed against the potentical economic impact on transaction costs.
